name: Hormah
overview: Hormah was a city located southwest of the Dead Sea, known for being the site of significant conflict between Israel and the Canaanite inhabitants. Scripture records that the tribes of Judah and Simeon captured Hormah, which was allotted to Simeon within the territory of Judah. The name Hormah means 'Utter destruction,' reflecting the complete defeat of the Canaanites there, as Israel vowed to destroy their cities and the LORD granted them victory. This city and its king are mentioned in the context of Israel’s conquest and the fulfillment of God's promises to His people.
